functions.description: Normalize raw project cash flow inputs into a positive outlay, numeric inflow, numeric salvage, decimal discount rate, and integer project life.
inputs: the initial investment outlay at time zero with currency unit
the annual cash inflow received at the end of each year with currency unit
the project life in whole years over which annual inflows and salvage occur
the salvage value received at the end of the project life with currency unit
the discount rate as a percentage or decimal for the project cash flows
outputs: the initial outlay as a positive amount
the annual cash inflow as a number
the salvage value as a number
the discount rate as a decimal
the project life as an integer number of years

functions.description: Compute the discount factor (1+r)^-n for a decimal discount rate and a number of periods.
inputs: the discount rate as a decimal
the number of periods until the cash is received
outputs: the discount factor for the given periods

functions.description: Compute the annuity present value factor for a decimal discount rate and a number of periods.
inputs: the discount rate as a decimal
the number of periods until the cash is received

functions.description: Compute the present value of a level annuity of equal end-of-period cash payments over a given number of periods.
inputs: the annual cash inflow as a number
the discount rate as a decimal
the project life as an integer number of years
outputs: the present value of the annual inflows

functions.description: Compute the present value of a single future cash amount received after a given number of periods.
inputs: the salvage value as a number
the discount rate as a decimal
the project life as an integer number of years
outputs: the present value of the salvage value

functions.description: Compute the net present value by summing the present values of future inflows and subtracting the initial outlay.
inputs: the initial outlay as a positive amount
the present value of the annual inflows
the present value of the salvage value
outputs: the net present value of the project

functions.description: Apply the accept-if-positive decision rule to a net present value.
inputs: the net present value of the project

functions.description: Evaluate the net present value of a project with an upfront outlay, level annual inflows, and a salvage value, then decide whether to accept it.
inputs: the initial investment outlay at time zero with currency unit
the annual cash inflow received at the end of each year with currency unit
the project life in whole years over which annual inflows and salvage occur
the salvage value received at the end of the project life with currency unit
the discount rate as a percentage or decimal for the project cash flows
outputs: the net present value of the project

entry_points.text: A project costs ●1 upfront and returns ●2 at the end of each year for ●3 years, plus a ●4 salvage value at the end of year ●3. At a discount rate of ●5, what is the NPV, and should the project be accepted?

params.description: the initial investment outlay at time zero with currency unit
params.validity_range: Must be a non-negative monetary amount, normally strictly positive for a real project; zero means no upfront cost and a negative value would be a cash inflow at time zero, which breaks the standard outlay interpretation.

params.description: the annual cash inflow received at the end of each year with currency unit
params.validity_range: Must be a real monetary amount, typically non-negative; a value of zero gives an annuity of nothing, and negative values represent net outflows each year, which the same formula still handles mathematically.

params.description: the project life in whole years over which annual inflows and salvage occur
params.validity_range: Must be a positive integer (at least 1) because the formulas discount discrete end-of-year periods from year 1 through year n; fractional or zero lives are not meaningful under this model.

params.description: the salvage value received at the end of the project life with currency unit
params.validity_range: Must be a non-negative monetary amount; zero means no salvage, and a negative value would represent a closure cost paid at the end of the project, which the same discounting formula still accommodates.

params.description: the discount rate as a percentage or decimal for the project cash flows
params.validity_range: Must be greater than -100% so that the discount factor (1+r) raised to the power of the period count is defined and nonzero; in practice a non-negative rate, typically between 0% and 100%, is used, and the rate must be expressed consistently as a decimal in the formulas.

entry_points.text: A project costs $120,000 upfront and returns $35,000 at the end of each year for 5 years, plus a $10,000 salvage value at the end of year 5. At a discount rate of 8%, what is the NPV, and should the project be accepted?
